question.text: Mr. Anil Kumar's Cat II 'Saraswati Infra Debt Trust' is considering investing in Securitised Debt Instruments (SDIs). Per Chapter 9, SDIs were introduced by SEBI in __ under which regulation, and what is the defining feature of an SDI structure?

answer.text: 2008; SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations; an SDI is almost similar to an SPV that pools funds to invest in assets leasable to a target company, providing fixed lease-based income to investors.
2012; SEBI (AIF) Regulations; an SDI is a synthetic derivative linked to the Nifty-50.
2015; SEBI (REIT) Regulations; an SDI is a pass-through trust for listed real-estate rentals.
2020; SEBI (InvIT) Regulations; an SDI is a power-sector financing instrument only.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'SDI was introduced by SEBI in 2008 under the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations. An SDI is almost similar to a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), which is created with the sole intention of pooling funds and investing in assets that can be further leased on to a target company.' The Trap: Options B/C/D invent wrong years and wrong regulations. The 2008 SDI regulation is a specific SEBI framework and is commonly confused with REIT (2014) and InvIT (2014). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covered SDI under all-cat. XIX-A tests SDI at distributor level. XXI-B (PM) does not typically use SDI since PMs handle listed securities primarily. Manager's Pro-Tip: For SDI exposure in a Cat II debt AIF, obtain both a credit rating (mandatory) and an independent lessor financial review. The sponsor's due diligence on the target company is your first line of default defence — document it in the IM.
